title: When the Semester Turns
premise: Jude Sandoval has spent three years perfecting invisibility at Hollow Creek High, channeling everything unsaid into the loaves she bakes at her family's panadería. But when the school's legendary ghost — the girl who died in the 1974 fire — begins leaving notes in ink that shifts like smoke, addressed to Jude by name, her careful anonymity unravels. The ghost isn't haunting; she's recruiting, and she knows Jude's grandmother was the fire's only survivor who never told the whole truth. As Jude digs into a cover-up that entwines her family's bakery, the school board, and the friends she never let herself have, she learns the ghost's notes are written in a dye her grandmother invented — and that inheritance means choosing which secrets to keep and which to burn. In the end, Jude exposes the truth at graduation, frees the ghost's story, and claims a found family that sees her fully — labels off, oven on.
about_author: August Reyes is the pen name of a former night-shift baker who wrote their first novel on flour-dusted receipt paper during closing shifts. They write stories about quiet kids, loud kitchens, and the ghosts we inherit from the people who love us.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. We meet Jude mid-semester: invisible by design, baking grief-bread after her grandmother's stroke, dodging her ex-best-friend Marisol in the halls. A routine day establishes the rules of her survival. Emotional beat: the ache of being safe and lonely at once.

chapters.title: The First Note
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A note appears inside her locker — 'Jude Sandoval. You bake what you can't say.' The ink shimmers like oil on water and won't smudge. She assumes a prank, but the handwriting matches the ghost stories told about the 1974 fire. Beat: a crack in the armor, fear laced with being seen.

chapters.title: Concha Logic
chapters.summary: Jude's POV at the panadería, with her father's POV interwoven. Dad notices the bread she's baking — angry sourdough, apology pan dulce — and says nothing, just leaves extra flour out. Jude tests the note's ink against every pen she owns. Beat: the family's wordless love, and the first pull of curiosity.

chapters.title: Marisol, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The ex-best-friend, now student council golden girl, catches Jude photographing the note and covers for her with a hall monitor. Old loyalty flickers. Marisol remembers the summer they stopped speaking — a secret Jude still doesn't know she knows. Beat: longing disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Yearbook
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Library research: Elena Vásquez, class of 1974, died in the gym fire, left behind a half-finished science fair project on 'living inks.' The ghost's notes match her handwriting exactly. Beat: the thrill of a real mystery, and the first dread that her family is in it.

chapters.title: What Abuela Kept
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Visiting her grandmother, half-lucid after the stroke, Jude finds a locked recipe box. Abuela murmurs Elena's name and a warning: 'Some bread is baked to forget.' Jude pockets a small brass key she finds taped beneath the box. Beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Second Note, Sharper Ink
chapters.summary: The ghost's POV, brief and lyrical. The ghost explains her rules: she can only write what someone in the building remembers wrongly. Her second note to Jude: 'Ask your grandmother what she carried out of the fire.' Beat: the ghost's loneliness mirrors Jude's.

chapters.title: The Study Group That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude and Theo's POV. Theo, a conspiracy-brained AV kid, catches Jude sneaking into the archive and insists on helping. Their banter is the first easy friendship she's had in years. Beat: found family begins as an accident of shared curiosity.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box Opens
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The brass key opens the box: Elena's ink formula, written as a recipe card in Abuela's hand, and a letter never sent — a confession that the fire was arson, and Abuela saw who set it. Beat: the floor drops out of Jude's family story.

chapters.title: Labels
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol confronts Jude: her grandfather was the school board president who buried the arson report, and she's known for years. The fight is ugly and true. 'You didn't lose me, Jude. You hid from me.' Beat: the cost of invisibility, finally named.

chapters.title: Smoke and Flour
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Someone ransacks the panadería looking for the recipe box. Dad is shaken; Abuela's health dips. Jude realizes the person who started the 1974 fire has a living stake in the cover-up — and is still in Hollow Creek. Beat: survival stops being passive.

chapters.title: Theo's Footage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Archive footage shows a teenage Abuela pulling Elena's project case from the flames — and a second figure watching. The figure's class ring matches the current vice principal's. Beat: the past and present collide; dread sharpens into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Bargain
chapters.summary: The ghost's POV. In the burned-out gym annex, Jude finally 'meets' Elena — a presence, a cold spot, a voice in the ink. Elena can't rest until the true report is read aloud on school grounds. She offers Jude the whole truth in exchange. Beat: awe, terror, and a choice taking shape.

chapters.title: What Dad Knew
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Dad confesses: he always knew Abuela carried Elena's work out, and built the bakery to honor a debt he never understood. The panadería's founding recipe is Elena's ink formula, baked into bread so it would survive. Beat: inheritance reframed as devotion, not burden.

chapters.title: Vice Principal Vega
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude and Marisol. Vega, grandson of the board president, corners Jude with a scholarship threat — stay quiet or lose college money. The price of survival is spelled out in dollars. Beat: the antagonist humanized and menacing; stakes become concrete.

chapters.title: The Plan, With Extra Hands
chapters.summary: Full ensemble POV rotation. Jude, Marisol, Theo, and Dad plan to read the recovered arson report aloud at graduation — legally, publicly, irrevocably. Marisol uses her council access; Theo handles broadcast; Jude bakes Elena's formula into the graduation bread. Beat: found family as strategy and warmth.

chapters.title: Vega's Countermove
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Vega suspends Marisol, raids the archive, and has the report 'misfiled.' The group's evidence vanishes overnight — except the copy baked into the recipe cards, which Vega doesn't know to look for. Beat: despair, then the quiet triumph of what was hidden in plain sight.

chapters.title: Abuela's Morning
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A lucid morning: Abuela tells the whole story — she and Elena were best friends, she fled the fire with the project, and she's spent fifty years baking the apology she never spoke. She gives Jude her blessing. Beat: the emotional heart of the book; grief and love in one kitchen.

chapters.title: Graduation Eve
chapters.summary: The ghost's POV and Jude's. Elena's presence is thinning as the truth nears daylight. She and Jude share a final 'conversation' through ink and flour dust. Elena asks not for vengeance, only to be remembered by name. Beat: tender, elegiac, the calm before the climax.

chapters.title: When the Semester Turns
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At graduation, mid-ceremony, the bread is distributed, the report is read aloud over the AV system, and Vega's family's cover-up collapses in front of the town. Jude stands at the mic — the invisible girl, visible at last. Beat: climax; fear transmuted into voice.

chapters.title: The Last Note
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In her empty locker, one final note in fading ink: 'Thank you, Jude Sandoval. Now I'm just a story, and you're the teller.' The ink goes still. The gym annex feels, for the first time, only like a building. Beat: release; grief and gratitude braided.

chapters.title: What We Bake Next
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, epilogue. Summer at the panadería: Marisol restocking shelves, Theo building a memorial display for Elena, Abuela teaching Jude the ink-recipe by heart. Jude writes her college essay — the true one. Beat: resolution; inheritance chosen, family found, the oven lit.
